title: The apparent board
blurb: Why unclaimed cards can't give check, how they can still defend, and why a bluffed check still counts.

steps.say: Check and checkmate are judged on the apparent board: claims count as if true. An unclaimed card can't give check yet. Move your king to e2, right in line with the card on e5. The card could be a rook or a queen, so he gets a chance to defend e2.
steps.success: He passed, so that card can't really reach e2. Safe, for now.

steps.say: He claimed Rook and now you're in check! A bluffed check is a real check until someone calls it. Do you believe him? Call!
steps.hint: Press Call in the bar under the board.
steps.success: It was a bishop pretending to be a rook. Claiming early gives a piece power, but it also gives you something to call.

steps.say: Now the other side. Take the pawn on c2 with your king. Nothing on the apparent board guards it, but the card on b4 could, if it's really a knight.
steps.success: He defended: the card was a knight, and it guards c2. Your king goes back, the pawn returns, you pay a chip and lose your turn. A king that walks next to unclaimed cards is gambling.
